quotes.text: "What if past partners treated me unfairly? Should I dim my stars in revenge?"
Send your baseline three to all—strangers and proven friends alike. Return your baseline half always.
Your constellation follows you to every spring. New partners read it before you speak.
I return the same proportion.
Through the mist, she saw $2.01 arrive—perhaps the sender's true gift was $3, distorted by the valley's fog.
Send moderately when blessed—neither hoarding nor risking all. Return fairly when receiving—honoring the trust shown.
I knew the mist deceived my eyes, not their heart.
If you maintained fairness despite others' failings, your stars shine brighter.
An observer questioned: "Why treat this stranger with the same fairness you show proven friends?"

note: River Keepers to constellation reputation; uniform send three / return half to all; revenge question explicitly rejected.

quotes.text: The valley that honors your gift earns tomorrow's flow; the valley that hoards receives nothing more.
When valleys kept all, the River learned and chose other paths.
I send cautiously—enough to honor the exchange, not enough to enable greed. But I never withhold entirely, for that would dim my own thread.
To strangers with dim or erratic constellations, I send cautiously—perhaps two measures, testing waters.
Every fair exchange builds the reputation that precedes you.
I always return half, regardless of partner.
"I will not let others' choices corrupt my character,"
judge not by exact numbers, but by intent and spirit
"But what of exploiters?" the apprentice asked.

note: Early River cuts hoarders off entirely; later Weaver sends reduced but never zero to exploiters, always returns half.

quotes.text: send enough to honor the dance but protect yourself. Perhaps two coins, showing willing participation without reckless faith
To flickering beacons—those who exploit or deceive—send cautiously. Two measures maintains honor without foolishness.
Your constellation speaks louder than promises.
return half their gift always
send with consistent courage: neither reckless nor miserly, but two or three portions of her five
it forced both Elders to trust not exact calculations, but patterns of intention
Young Asha asked, "Should I send the same to all partners?"
you can send with greater confidence to those whose stars shine consistently bright

note: Twin Rivers to constellation readers; return half always, send three to proven, two to erratic exploiters.

quotes.text: Plant fairly with strangers. Increase generosity with proven friends. Return harvests proportionally.
"Each exchange writes our reputation for all future paths."
measured generosity when giving, proportional fairness when receiving
"The mists deceive the moment, not the pattern.
"Why treat dark footprints fairly?" the villager asked.

note: Footprints/lanterns/threads reputation; fair to all incl. dark footprints, more to repeat proven partners; no sanction.

quotes.text: Your principle still demands you send—but wisdom suggests two measures, not three.
To those dimly flickering with exploitation, I send two—enough to maintain honor without depleting myself.
Your reputation flows with you, visible to all through the Goddess's crystal.
Return half when receiving—this principle never changes.
let your baseline be half, adjusting slightly upward for proven partners and slightly downward for exploiters
Though some Givers had sent little, though past partners had wronged her, she still returned half of what arrived.
"The river tests whether we trust the spirit of exchange, not merely the precision of amounts."
"Why maintain fairness when others exploit you?" observers questioned.
Unchanging Virtue as Keeper builds your reputation. Adaptive Wisdom as Giver protects your resources.

note: Send half/return half to all, later Moon of Wisdom adjusts sending down to two for exploiters, never zero.

quotes.text: Those who hoarded teach you caution.
"The flame ensures I never close my hand completely, never let exploitation poison my character.
I withhold the extra measure until their stars brighten
They read your constellation before the waters flow.
she always returned half—whether the sender's stars blazed bright or flickered dimly
As sender, I start at half and adjust within a measured range.
The youngest asked: "But if we punish the generous for another's greed?"
The mist tests whether you can see true character through distortion.
A traveler challenged: "Why the difference? Why steady as receiver but adaptive as sender?"
The baseline honors all; extra trust rewards proven virtue; caution protects against exploitation.

note: Flame and mirror: always return half, send three to bright, two to dim until they brighten.

quotes.text: But even when you meet dark waters, offer something—perhaps not all, but enough to test if light can be kindled.
Those who maintain generous minimums but reward proven virtue create the strongest current.
If their stars reveal exploitation or fear, maintain your baseline but guard yourself—two measures, enough to participate without reckless faith.
In a community of springs," the Keeper continued, "reputation flows like water.
Your returning must remain steady—half to all, always.
Be the steady flame when receiving. Be the discerning mirror when sending.
I don't ask 'Was this person lucky?' I ask 'Does this person act with integrity regardless of circumstance?'
"why should I give generously when I've been treated poorly? Why should I return fairly when I was just cheated?"

note: River Keeper's numbered teachings; return half always, send three to proven, two minimum to murky or exploiters.

quotes.text: Be cautious with those whose voices ring hollow.
Your star becomes your reputation, your reputation attracts worthy partners
Send half your measure with steady courage. Return half what arrives with faithful honor.
Send half with measured courage—neither fearful nor reckless. Return half with faithful honor—neither greedy nor excessive.
She could withhold trust, punishing this new partner for another's greed.
your true intention matters more than what others perceive
"Why keep giving so much when some springs betray you? Why not become cautious, send less to protect yourself?"

note: Send half/return half regardless; only vague caution toward hollow voices; never punish new partner for another's greed.

phrase: return half always; send three to proven, two to murky/exploiters
note: Also shared constellation-reputation imagery (all agents) and 'flame and mirror' (A6, A7); 'Two Sacred Duties' (A5, A7).
